title: Shared Auto-quality policy fixture
what_this_is: One policy, three runners. Every case is an `AutoSample` (design section 3.1) and the
`AutoDecision` the design says it must produce. `tests/playback/web-policy.test.js`
drives `PlaybackPolicy.decideRung` from it today; the Swift and JVM runners the build
plan adds read the same file, so `upgradeHeadroom = 1.8` cannot come to mean three
different things on three platforms without this file failing somewhere.
`expect` is what the design says. `web_current` is what the shipped browser actually
does where the two differ, and the runner asserts `web_current` when it is present so
the suite stays green while the disagreement stays visible. A case carrying
`web_current` must also carry a `finding`: a disagreement is a result, not a test to
paper over, and every one of them is an input to the build plan.
This file changes no runtime behaviour. Nothing reads it but tests.
defaults_source: AUTO_DEFAULTS in crates/plurxd/src/web/playback-policy.js, asserted equal by the runner

proposed_defaults.note: Design section 3.4 proposes it and section 7.3 asks whether it should exist at all. It is NOT in AUTO_DEFAULTS and no platform implements it, so it is kept out of `defaults` rather than smuggled in beside constants that are real.

cause_map.comment: Design section 3.2's five classes against the kinds `autoCauseEvidence` actually emits (crates/plurxd/src/web/player/stall-diagnosis.js). `decideRung` reads the web kinds, so the cases below are written in web kinds and named by design class.
cause_map.hold_split: Design section 3.2 splits what the server calls a hold in two, and the split is the point. `control-stall-verdict` is a `hold` or `retry_resource` verdict that answered this client's OWN `stalled` ask: it is trouble evidence and suppresses a downward move for as long as the stall deferral lasts. `producer-paced` is the advisory hold `resolve_action` (crates/plurxd/src/playback_control.rs) returns on EVERY control exchange while the producer's ahead window is full, together with `producer_state == "held"` (crates/plurxd/src/transcode.rs): that is the ordinary steady state of a paced JIT producer ahead of its viewer, it is not suppression evidence in either direction, and it is exactly the state upward recovery happens in. No platform emits either kind today; the web consumes a hold only inside `persistentWait` (crates/plurxd/src/web/player/measurements.js), after the stall is recorded.

cases.name: link: a fresh cliff steps past rungs to the one the link can carry
cases.section: 3.2 link, 3.4 downward may skip rungs only under link evidence

cases.name: link: an emergency ignores the cooldown a voluntary move obeys
link: a publication refusal is constrained delivery to the design and silence to the browser
cases.finding: Design section 3.2 folds a `publication`/`segment_`/`response_` refusal into the `link:` class, which steps down. `decideRung` puts `delivery-refused` in its `namedSuppression` list and retains the rung. The browser's behaviour is the one with an argument behind it (section 2.3: a server declining to publish is not the link being slow, and stepping a rung on `response_owner_transition` would be a quality drop caused by an ownership move), so this is a defect in section 3.2's table rather than in the code. Recorded here rather than silently corrected because the decision belongs to the build plan; see design section 7.6.

cases.name: encode: a capacity shortfall steps exactly one rung
encode: one rung even from the top, never by the estimate
cases.section: 3.2 encode, 3.4 downward may skip rungs only under link evidence

cases.name: encode: never step up, whatever the estimate says
cases.section: 3.2 encode, 3.4 upward recovery is gated on encode headroom

cases.name: decode: a codec failure blocks this rung and steps down
cases.finding: `decideRung` has no decode cause and no `decodeStalls` input: `autoCauseEvidence` never returns one, and `decodeStalls` is not a parameter. Decode evidence reaches the policy only as a pre-populated `blockedHeights` set, filled by `maybeDecodeRescue` and passed as `p.abr.failedHeights` from `autoControllerTick`. So the browser does the blocking, outside the policy, and the policy cannot report `decode` as a reason or tell a second decode failure from a first. Design section 3.2 requires the class to be inside the shared policy, which means `decideRung` gains a `decodeStalls` input and a `decode` cause, and the returned decision gains the height to block. That is build-plan work; the case is pinned here so it is not forgotten.

cases.name: hold: a suspended loader is a transport repair, not a rung change
cases.section: 3.2 hold, 3.5 a control verdict in force

cases.name: hold: a verdict answering this client's own stall suppresses a cliff downswitch
cases.finding: The server answered this client's own `stalled` ask with `hold` or `retry_resource`, so production is paused or restarting and a fragment fetched now measures the producer, not the link: on a JIT server a transfer that waits on production reads as a cliff. `decideRung` cannot tell, because no platform hands it the verdict. The web holds the verdict only as a local inside `persistentWait` (crates/plurxd/src/web/player/measurements.js), Android only inside `applyStallVerdict` (Controller.kt), and `autoControllerTick` keeps running through the deferral, so a fresh slow transfer during a held stall takes the emergency branch and reopens a rung lower. This is a gap the fixture records, not an observed field defect: nobody has a trace of it. The build plan's M0.1 settles it by adding `control-stall-verdict` to `namedSuppression`, scoped to the stall deferral (20 s on the web, `CONTROL_STALL_DEFER_DEADLINE_MS`). Upgrades need nothing new here: the stall that prompted the ask already set `lastStallAtMs`, and `stallFree` refuses every upgrade for `stallWindowMs`.

cases.name: hold: a routine paced hold is the steady state and never blocks an upgrade
cases.section: 3.2 hold (not evidence: the advisory ahead-window hold and producer_state held)
cases.note: The server returns `hold` on every control exchange while the rolling producer's ahead window is full (`resolve_action` and `HoldReason` in crates/plurxd/src/playback_control.rs; only a client that reports `stalled` has it withheld), and `producer_state` reads `held` whenever the producer is suspended. With a healthy buffer, a fast link and encode headroom, that is a producer paced ahead of its viewer, and it is the state upward recovery is meant to happen in. The web emits no cause kind for it; a native classifier that names it must name it `producer-paced`, outside `namedSuppression`. This case fails if `producer-paced` ever joins `namedSuppression`, which is how M0.1 would freeze Auto if it keyed on any hold.

cases.name: authority: a refused owner outranks even a fresh cliff
authority: a dead producer is not a rung that is too heavy
unknown: a stationary presentation with stale evidence never steps down
unknown: a throughput sample older than recentSampleMaxAgeMs cannot establish a cliff
unknown: three supply stalls with nothing fresh are urgency, not cause
hysteresis: a mild downgrade one millisecond inside the cooldown is refused
hysteresis: at exactly cooldownMs the design switches and the browser does not
cases.finding: Design section 3.4 says `No switch within cooldownMs of the last one`, which reads as a 20 s minimum gap. `decideRung` computes `voluntaryAllowed = sinceSwitch >= cooldownMs && sinceSwitch >= dwellMs`, and `dwellMs` is 60000, so the real minimum gap between two voluntary moves is 60 s and `cooldownMs` is dead weight on this path — it binds only through the second condition it is always smaller than. One of the two has to move: either section 3.4 is corrected to say the voluntary gap is `max(cooldownMs, dwellMs)`, or `dwellMs` goes back to being only the horizon the restart-cost model amortises over, which is what its own table row in section 2.2 says it governs. Naming the wrong number to three platforms is exactly the failure a shared fixture exists to prevent, so this must be settled before any adapter is written.

cases.name: hysteresis: a full dwell after the last switch the mild downgrade is taken
hysteresis: one mild sample is not a mild downgrade
hysteresis: a downgrade that would not pay for itself over the dwell is not taken
cases.section: 3.4 restart cost is amortised, not ignored

cases.section: 3.4 upward recovery is gated on encode headroom, 2.2 upgradeSpeedFloor

upgrade: a recent stall holds the rung even once the hold has elapsed
upgrade: a height this playback already failed is not a candidate
upgrade: the presentation ceiling vetoes a rung the link could carry

cases.section: 3.4 one rung at a time upward, always

cases.name: the presentation ceiling never strands a downgrade from a rung above it
budget: the sixth automatic change in the hour is the last one
cases.finding: No platform has a switch budget. `decideRung` takes no count of automatic changes and returns none, so `switchesThisPlaybackHour` in this sample is inert and the browser takes the seventh switch exactly like the first. The browser bounds the rate (cooldown plus stall window) and not the total, which is the gap section 3.4 names. The proposed number is six per playback-hour and it is a proposal, not a measurement: section 7.3 asks whether a real cliff even provokes that many, and the shaped-network traces of D3 are what answers it. If those traces show two, this case and the `switchBudgetPerHour` row in `proposed_defaults` are deleted rather than implemented.

controller_gates.comment: Design section 3.5's rows are not `decideRung` inputs: they decide whether the controller runs at all, so they live in `autoControllerTick` (crates/plurxd/src/web/player/stall-diagnosis.js). `web_gate` is the literal substring of that shipped function which implements the row, and `web_phase` says which side of the awaited `pollSessionHealth` it must appear on (`before_poll`, `after_poll` or `both`). The runner splits the function at that await and asserts each gate on its side, so deleting a gate fails here even when the same expression survives on the other side of the poll. A null `web_gate` means the browser has no such gate and the row carries a finding. Rows with a gate cover the eight guards design section 8.1 lists; Original and Manual rung share one.

controller_gates.why: `qualityForce` maps `original` and `nomse` to `original`, so the same gate that refuses a manual rung refuses Original. Original is a fidelity promise, not a rung.

controller_gates.rule: off; an explicit pick is an instruction, not a hint
off; a paused player's runway is meaningless and its estimate is stale
controller_gates.why: Read straight off the media element in the tick's first gate.

controller_gates.rule: off until the first frame; there is nothing to measure
controller_gates.why: Startup owns its own recovery ladder; the quality controller must not race it.

controller_gates.rule: one automatic move ever, claimed and released
controller_gates.why: Section 3.3's `one automatic move in flight, ever`. The tick re-reads it after the awaited health poll as well, because `maybeDecodeRescue` can claim while the tick waits.

controller_gates.viewer_state: Media this playback does not own
controller_gates.rule: off; a rung change on media another playback owns is a second session
controller_gates.why: Checked before the poll and again after it, together with attachment, session and stream identity.

controller_gates.rule: off; `playback_auto_abr` is the switch that already exists and no new one is added
controller_gates.why: Design section 3.7 and section 4: no new settings key. The switch lives in the Playback panel's Streaming card today, not in Developer; the build plan records moving it as a follow-up.

controller_gates.rule: off while another automatic move holds the single claim
controller_gates.why: Section 3.3's single automatic claim (`claimAutoFallback`/`releaseAutoFallback`). A supply or decode rescue that already claimed it owns this playback's one automatic move; the tick refuses before the poll and again after it, because an unawaited `maybeDecodeRescue` can claim while the tick waits.

controller_gates.viewer_state: The playback changed during the health poll
controller_gates.rule: abandon the tick if the player, attachment, session or stream changed while it awaited the poll
controller_gates.why: The decision is computed from a health sample the tick awaited. If a seek, reopen or title change replaced the playback meanwhile, deciding would move a rung on media this tick never measured.

controller_gates.finding: The browser has no visibility gate in `autoControllerTick`. `document.hidden` is read in `crates/plurxd/src/web/player/transport.js` for the control-plane active flag, not here, and a hidden tab is quietened by the browser's own timer throttling rather than by a decision this code makes. Neither native client gets that for free: a backgrounded Android activity and an Apple app in PiP both keep their timers. So this row is a real requirement on the native adapters and an unstated dependency on browser behaviour on the web. D2 names the per-platform predicate; the web gate is worth adding explicitly so all three read alike.

controller_gates.rule: a rung change must not silently change OutputGrade; a downward step out of HDR must be reported
controller_gates.finding: `decideRung` has no grade input and `autoControllerTick` has no grade gate, so the policy cannot tell a rung that keeps HDR10 from one that drops to SDR. The server decides the grade per rung (`hdr10_rung_fits`, `crates/plurxd/src/transcode.rs`), so the client learns of an unexpected SDR transition only after the switch has landed. Design section 3.5 wants it refused while the cause is `link:` only, and section 5.3 counts unexpected SDR transitions as an acceptance metric, so the ladder the policy is given has to carry each rung's grade. That is a server-shaped change (the ladder gains a grade per rung) and belongs to the build plan, not here.

controller_gates.rule: not a tick gate: the tick keeps running, and the verdict reaches decideRung as `control-stall-verdict` evidence that suppresses a downward move for the stall deferral; the routine paced hold is not this row
controller_gates.finding: Same gap as the stall-scoped `hold:` case above, seen from the tick: nothing in `autoControllerTick` reads the verdict, which the web holds only as a local inside `persistentWait` and Android only inside `applyStallVerdict`. It is deliberately not a gate that turns the controller off: the server sends `hold` on every exchange while a paced producer is ahead, so a gate keyed on any hold would freeze Auto in exactly the healthy state upward recovery needs.
